```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(httr2)
library(purrr)
```

```{r}
#| cache: true

years <- c(2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022)

urls <- c(
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20150101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20170101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20190101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20210101/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/",
  "https://web.archive.org/web/20220201012049/https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/"
)

# Fetch one Wayback IMDb Top 250 page and return a tidy 250-row tibble
scrape_snapshot <- \(url, snap_year) {
  page <- request(url) |>
    req_timeout(90) |>
    req_retry(max_tries = 3) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_html()

  # Pull vote counts from rating tooltips ("9.2 based on 1,354,030 votes")
  votes <- page |>
    html_elements("td.ratingColumn.imdbRating strong") |>
    html_attr("title") |>
    str_remove(".*based on ") |>
    parse_number()

  page |>
    html_element("table") |>
    html_table() |>
    select(`Rank & Title`, rating = `IMDb Rating`) |>
    # Split "1.\n    The Shawshank Redemption\n    (1994)" into rank, title, year
    separate_wider_regex(
      `Rank & Title`,
      patterns = c(
        "^\\s*",
        rank = "\\d+",
        "\\.\\s+",
        title = ".*",
        "\\s+\\(",
        year = "\\d{4}",
        "\\)\\s*$"
      )
    ) |>
    mutate(
      snap_year = snap_year,
      rank = as.integer(rank),
      year = as.integer(year),
      number = votes
    ) |>
    select(snap_year, rank, title, year, rating, number)
}

# Scrape all five snapshots in parallel pairs and stack into one tibble
imdb_snapshots <- map2(urls, years, scrape_snapshot) |>
  list_rbind()
```

```{r}
rank_changes <- imdb_snapshots |>
  filter(snap_year %in% c(2015, 2022)) |>
  select(title, year, snap_year, rank) |>
  # Put 2015 and 2022 ranks in separate columns for each film
  pivot_wider(names_from = snap_year, values_from = rank, names_prefix = "rank_") |>
  # Keep only films present in both snapshots
  drop_na(rank_2015, rank_2022) |>
  # Positive = moved up toward #1; negative = dropped in rank
  mutate(rank_change = rank_2015 - rank_2022)

rank_changes |>
  arrange(desc(abs(rank_change))) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```

```{r}
rank_changes <- rank_changes |>
  # Floor release year to its decade (e.g., 1994 -> 1990)
  mutate(decade = (year %/% 10) * 10)

rank_changes |>
  summarize(avg_rank_change = mean(rank_change), .by = decade) |>
  arrange(decade)
```

```{r}
imdb_snapshots |>
  # Count appearances per film (include year since remakes can share a title)
  count(title, year, name = "n_snapshots") |>
  # Distribution of how many snapshots films appear in
  count(n_snapshots, name = "n_films")
```

```{r}
rank_changes |>
  summarize(avg_rank_change = mean(rank_change), .by = decade) |>
  arrange(decade) |>
  mutate(
    decade_label = factor(paste0(decade, "s"), levels = paste0(decade, "s")),
    direction = if_else(avg_rank_change > 0, "Rose", "Fell")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = avg_rank_change, y = decade_label, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  # Vertical reference line marking zero net rank change
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Rose" = "#1b9e77", "Fell" = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(
    title = "Older Classics Lost Ground in the IMDb Top 250 (2015–2022)",
    subtitle = "Average change in rank by release decade; only 1990s films gained spots on average",
    x = "Average Rank Change (Spots Moved Toward #1)",
    y = "Release Decade",
    fill = "Rank Direction",
    caption = "Source: IMDb Top 250 via Wayback Machine (190 films appear in both the 2015 and 2022 snapshots)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
